correctness.rationale: For a smooth quartic K3 S⊂P³, its affine 3-fold cone has a unique vertex singularity of order 4, and blowing up the vertex gives Tot(O_S(−1)) with smooth exceptional E=S and maximal-ideal order m_E=1. In a local cone chart x_i=t s_i(u,v), the Gauss three-plane depends only on (u,v); ambient Jacobian 3×3 minors of the blow-up differential have exact order t², giving Mather discrepancy k^hat_E=2. The sourced Ratajczak Thm 1.2 exponent α_E=k^hat_E+1−3m_E=0 yields Θ=(L−1)[S]/(L³−1)=[S]/(1+L+L²), after checking the denominator is invertible in the stated localization. If two densities agree, multiplying by invertible [P²] equates [S] and [T] in the localized Grothendieck ring. The alternating rational mixed-Hodge realization reduces their difference to [H²(S,Q)]−[H²(T,Q)]. Finite-weight graded Grothendieck classes admit injective multiplication by (1−Q(−j)) or its negative-weight counterpart (check extremal support), and rational pure polarizable Hodge structures are semisimple; thus this equality forces an unpolarized rational Hodge isomorphism, hence equal Picard ranks via Lefschetz (1,1). Fixing an unpolarized Q-Hodge structure restricts period lines to countably many GL22(Q) rational-marking images; local Torelli yields discrete, hence countable, fibers in a second-countable 19-dimensional moduli, so uncountably many Θ values. Ehresmann isotopy of the smooth quartic family and links of cones identifies topological germs; all multiplicity four. The rank 20 Fermat/rank 1 very general pair separates values. The general density formula and Torelli are credited inputs, not newly proved universal tools.
residual_risks: No converse: rational Hodge equality not claimed to imply motivic density equality; no preservation of polarizations, only unpolarized Q-Hodge.
The weight cancellation must occur in full K0(MHS_Q), not in numerical Hodge–Deligne polynomial; latter cannot distinguish K3 periods.
Source formula and chart normalizations matter; α_E=0 from verified Jacobian factor, not an unqualified general cone formula.

The density formula is inherited, but the Hodge realization cancellation and K3 period-fiber argument connect local motivic geometry to global rational Hodge periods.
